title: Story 1.2: Show last login on the My Account page
description:
# Story 1.2: Show last login on the My Account page

**Points:** 1 | **Role:** frontend | **Dependencies:** Story 1.1

## Context & Rationale
Surfaces the value Story 1.1 exposes. Display-only; no business logic in the view.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The customer info page shows "Last login: <date>" using the service method
  from Story 1.1, wired through a model factory (not queried in the view).
- Hidden entirely when the value is null rather than printing a blank row.
- The label is a `LocaleStringResource`, not a hardcoded string.
- The view override lives under `Themes/DefaultClean/Views/`, leaving the base
  `Views/` copy untouched.

## Files likely touched
- `src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Factories/CustomerModelFactory.cs`
- `src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Models/Customer/CustomerInfoModel.cs`
- `src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Themes/DefaultClean/Views/Customer/Info.cshtml`

title: Story 2.2: Show a popular badge on the product box
description:
# Story 2.2: Show a "popular" badge on the product box

**Points:** 2 | **Role:** frontend | **Dependencies:** Story 2.1

## Context & Rationale
Visual treatment for the signal Story 2.1 exposes, on catalogue listing pages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Product boxes render a "Popular" badge when the count from Story 2.1 exceeds
  a threshold read from the `Setting` table (not hardcoded).
- Badge text comes from a `LocaleStringResource`.
- Styling is added to the DefaultClean theme stylesheet; no inline styles.
- Renders correctly at mobile widths and when the badge is absent.

## Files likely touched
- `src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Factories/CatalogModelFactory.cs`
- `src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Themes/DefaultClean/Views/Catalog/`
- `src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Themes/DefaultClean/Content/`

title: Story 2.1: Add a product view-count service method
description:
# Story 2.1: Add a product view-count service method

**Points:** 2 | **Role:** backend | **Dependencies:** none

## Context & Rationale
Story 2.2 needs a cheap way to ask "is this product popular?". Reads must go
through a service and be cached — per the architecture reference, cache
invalidation belongs in an `IConsumer<EntityUpdated<Product>>`, not ad-hoc
`_cacheManager.Remove` calls.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A service method returns a view/order count for a product id.
- The result is cached via `ICacheManager` with a documented cache key.
- Invalidation happens through an event consumer, not inline removal.
- Returns 0 rather than throwing for an unknown product id.

## Files likely touched
- `src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Catalog/`
- `src/Libraries/Nop.Core/Caching/`

title: Story 1.1: Expose customer last-login timestamp from CustomerService
description:
# Story 1.1: Expose customer last-login timestamp from CustomerService

**Points:** 2 | **Role:** backend | **Dependencies:** none

## Context & Rationale
`Customer` already records `LastLoginDateUtc`, but nothing in the service layer
returns it in a display-ready form. Story 1.2 needs it for the My Account page.
Per the architecture reference, controllers must not touch `IRepository<T>` —
this has to go through `Nop.Services`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `ICustomerService` gains a method returning the customer's last-login time,
  converted to the store's timezone via `IDateTimeHelper`.
- Returns null/empty for a customer who has never logged in (first-time login).
- Implementation lives in `Nop.Services/Customers/CustomerService.cs`; no EF
  access is added to any controller.
- Unit test in `Nop.Services.Tests` covers the never-logged-in case.

## Files likely touched
- `src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Customers/ICustomerService.cs`
- `src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Customers/CustomerService.cs`
- `src/Tests/Nop.Services.Tests/Customers/`

title: Story 1.3: Make the account menu keyboard-navigable
description:
# Story 1.3: Make the account menu keyboard-navigable

**Points:** 2 | **Role:** frontend | **Dependencies:** none

## Context & Rationale
The customer account sidebar is mouse-only. This is presentation-layer work with
no service dependency, so it can start immediately and in parallel with backend
stories. Deliberately independent — it gives the frontend role ready work from
the first dispatch cycle.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Account menu items are reachable by Tab and activate on Enter/Space.
- A visible focus style is present, meeting WCAG AA contrast against the
  DefaultClean background.
- The currently-selected item is marked with `aria-current`.
- No change to routing or controller logic; view and stylesheet only.
- Override lives under `Themes/DefaultClean/`, leaving base `Views/` untouched.

## Files likely touched
- `src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Themes/DefaultClean/Views/Customer/`
- `src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Themes/DefaultClean/Content/styles.css`
